documentation.title: Documentation
documentation.subtitle: A developer reference for integrating Cloudinary image optimization with Angular 22.

whatIsCloudinary.title: What is Cloudinary?
whatIsCloudinary.body: Cloudinary is a cloud-based media management and delivery platform that stores master assets and generates transformed, cached variants on demand via URL parameters and official SDKs.

whyOptimization.title: Why Image Optimization Matters
whyOptimization.body: High-resolution images frequently represent the majority of a page's byte weight. Delivering modern formats, perceptual compression, and viewport-appropriate dimensions can help improve Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and reduce bandwidth usage, depending on the asset and network conditions.

angularIntegration.title: Integrating Cloudinary with Angular 22
angularIntegration.body: Install @cloudinary/url-gen and @cloudinary/ng. Use @cloudinary/url-gen to compose type-safe CloudinaryImage instances with Signals and services, and render them with @cloudinary/ng or native HTML img elements with explicit width and height attributes.

fAuto.title: How f_auto Works
fAuto.body: The f_auto delivery parameter instructs Cloudinary's CDN to inspect the incoming browser Accept header and automatically return the most efficient supported format such as AVIF or WebP, falling back to JPEG or PNG when needed.

qAuto.title: How q_auto Works
qAuto.body: Unlike a static quality percentage, q_auto analyzes each image's visual complexity to choose an optimal compression level. Presets include q_auto:best, q_auto:good, q_auto:eco, and q_auto:low.

modernFormats.title: WebP & AVIF Explained
modernFormats.body: WebP and AVIF are modern image codecs designed for the web. AVIF typically achieves higher compression efficiency for photographs, while WebP offers fast decoding and broad compatibility.

resizing.title: Safe Resizing with c_limit
resizing.body: Combining c_limit with w_<pixels> scales down oversized originals while preserving aspect ratio and never upscaling images that are already smaller than the target width.

responsive.title: Responsive Images with srcset & sizes
responsive.body: Generating multiple width variants via Cloudinary lets the browser pick the smallest candidate that matches the layout width and device pixel ratio, avoiding wasted mobile downloads.

metrics.title: Interpreting Optimization Metrics
metrics.body: Cloudinary Image Lab fetches both the untransformed original and the transformed resource via the Fetch API, measuring Blob.size and reading the actual Content-Type header. This guarantees metrics match what the browser actually receives.

usingLab.title: Using the Image Lab
usingLab.body: Pick a demo asset from the gallery, adjust format, quality, or max width in the right-hand panel, drag the Before & After divider to inspect visual quality, and copy the resulting URL or Angular code.

cloudName.title: Configuring Your Own Cloud Name
cloudName.body: Update cloudName in src/environments/environment.ts and src/environments/environment.prod.ts (or provide CLOUDINARY_CONFIG). Replace the demo public IDs in src/app/core/constants/demo-images.constant.ts with assets from your own Cloudinary product environment.

security.title: Security Considerations
security.body: A Cloudinary Cloud Name is public by design for asset delivery. Never place your API Secret or signed Admin credentials in frontend code. If you add uploads later, use a restricted unsigned upload preset or a dedicated backend signing endpoint.

performance.title: Performance Best Practices
performance.body: Set explicit width and height attributes to prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS), reserve loading='lazy' for off-screen images only, cache measured transformation results, and cancel stale requests when users adjust controls rapidly.
